title: Are Your Fairness Metrics Accurate? A Semi-Supervised Approach to Improving Fairness Estimates Under Sample Selection Bias

problem.claim: Fairness metrics computed from observed data may be inaccurate when the labeled data is affected by selection bias or distributional shift.

gap.claim: Existing assumptions that observed-data fairness metrics are accurate do not address systematic, application-specific estimation errors under selection bias.

contributions.claim: The authors introduce SCC-invariance, a selection bias model for flexibly capturing distributional shifts in real-world data.

Under finite Gaussian mixture assumptions for each class-conditional distribution, the authors derive an Expectation-Maximization algorithm to estimate model parameters and correction weights for unbiased fairness estimates.
The authors apply the bias mitigation approach to fairness assessment of pathogenicity predictors across ancestral groups in clinical genetics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe SCC-invariance as a novel selection bias model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report improved estimates for equal opportunity, predictive equality, and predictive parity on synthetic data.
The authors report applying the approach to study fairness of pathogenicity predictors across ancestral groups in clinical genetics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Statistical bias in data can impair machine-learning deployment and differentially affect population groups.
Accurate fairness-metric estimation is important, but observed-data estimates can contain systematic errors under selection bias.
The work uses unbiased unlabeled data, introduces SCC-invariance, and derives an EM-based correction procedure.
The approach is evaluated for three fairness metrics on synthetic data.
The approach is applied to clinical-genetics predictors across ancestral groups.

source_observation.claim: Fairness estimates can be systematically distorted when labeled data is selected non-representatively.

interpretation.claim: Fairness evaluation should account for the data-selection process instead of assuming observed samples provide accurate metric estimates.

application.claim: When unbiased unlabeled data is available, semi-supervised correction may improve fairness estimates under selection bias.

exception.claim: The abstract specifies assumptions including access to unbiased unlabeled data and finite Gaussian mixture class-conditional distributions.

unknowns: No quantitative results or comparison baselines are reported.
The abstract does not specify the synthetic-data configuration or clinical-genetics dataset details.
The abstract does not establish performance beyond the reported author experiments.
